answer: 100 compute-hours are burned per identity to navigate a karst-like graph of logic gates, where an inlet of tasks requires a cryptographic quill to sign valid proofs. An arbiter enforces this via serial dependency; the honest cost is 1,000 units, while 1,000 fakes incur 100,000, as parallel work cannot bypass the forced serial dependency of the proof-path. Evidence of reuse triggers a permanent stake-lock. Fakes cannot be amortized because the state update is strictly exclusive to one identity at a time, ensuring each agent remains a verifiable, distinct repair node for the network.
